_doc: The Gym — a general pack (no cultural gate). Authored 2026-08-27. Shipped WITHOUT a prize board, deliberately and with the diagnostic recorded: every six-letter gym word is either over the 110-answer cap (PLATES, 136) or carries at most one on-theme row (CABLES, TOWELS, STRAIN). AUTHORING.md's 'too narrow to carry a pack' test therefore fires. The first attempt overrode it on counter-evidence and MEASURED 0.533 — below the floor and worse than laundry, which was cut. The diagnostic was right. This pack is the repair: exactly six free bases in the 2252-base pool can carry gym at all — POSTER at 4 named/said rows and five at 3 — and the pack uses five of them. The sixth, CORPSE, is tone-denied as a prize word by data/base-tone-deny.txt — the repo had already ruled that a word game does not open a board on that, and it was picked here on arithmetic alone. Dropping it also resolved a frequency-cap failure, because rope fell from four boards to three, which is the cap: a vocabulary this thin reuses the same rows. Clue gate for a general pack is binding: every clue names a position, a time, or a habit, never a category.

theme.name: The Gym
theme.blurb: The one on the corner with the handwritten sign, where somebody knows how long you have been coming.

boards.scene: The wall by the free weights

clues.poster: Curling at one corner since before you joined, and nobody will be the one to take it down
clues.reps: Counted out loud by the last three, and silently by everybody else
clues.rest: Ninety seconds that becomes four minutes once the phone comes out
clues.rope: Hung from the frame, and used the right way by maybe two people here
clues.spot: What you ask a stranger for, and what nobody has ever refused
clues.step: Boxed, stacked by the mirror, and dragged out for the one class on Tuesdays

boards.scene: The man who has been coming here since 1994

clues.master: What thirty years in one building makes somebody, whether or not anybody says it
clues.arms: The day of the week that never gets skipped, unlike the other one
clues.rest: Ninety seconds by the clock on the wall, timed exactly, every single set
clues.mat: His own, rolled under one arm, never the ones by the door
clues.steam: What comes off the towel he leaves folded on the bench between sets
clues.team: What he calls the four regulars on the platform, and nobody corrects him

boards.scene: The block on the whiteboard, week four of six

clues.period: Four weeks on the board, and the reason this month feels harder than last
clues.drop: What the last inch of the last one does, no matter the intention
clues.rope: Left on the high pulley by whoever finished before you, every single time
clues.dip: Between the bars, and the one everybody claims is easy until week four
clues.ride: Twenty minutes at the end that used to be the whole session
clues.pride: What week five costs, and what week six quietly gives back

clues.powder: Two scoops in the bottom of a bottle that has smelled like this since March
clues.drop: What the bar does the last inch of the last one, no matter the intention
clues.rope: Clipped to the high pulley, and left there by whoever went before you
clues.rod: The pin through the stack, and the reason the whole machine waits on one person
clues.row: Seated, elbows in, and the one thing the sign on the wall says you are doing wrong
clues.wore: What the grip tape did on the left side only, which tells you something

boards.scene: The rack by the door, in whatever order it was left

clues.tramps: What the treadmill row sounds like from the office upstairs at six in the morning
clues.strap: Looped twice at the wrist by everybody pulling more than their grip allows
clues.arms: Two of the five days, and the two nobody has ever needed reminding about
clues.mat: Rolled, unrolled, and never quite put back where the sign shows
clues.ramp: Up the last two weeks of a cycle, and the part people rush
clues.star: Drawn on the whiteboard beside whoever hit something that morning
